entry.title: After Antalya, Hope Is Not a Luxury
entry.summary:
VICTORIA, Seychelles, November 24 (IPS) - I left Copenhagen in December 2009 with a heavy heart. I had gone there as President of a small island nation, carrying the hopes of a people whose future is tied to the ocean around them. We had been told that this would be the summit that saved the planet. Instead, it ended in division and recrimination. Outside, in the freezing streets, thousands of young people and ordinary citizens had marched and pleaded for action. Inside, in the warm negotiating halls, we let them down.

entry.title: Security Council LIVE: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?
entry.summary:
When the UN was founded in 1945, computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is already assisting in targeting, drones are reshaping warfare and disinformation is spreading in unprecedented ways, fuelling record levels of conflict. The Security Council on Tuesday is weighing these changes, with UN chief António Guterres telling ambassadors, “killer robots must have no place in our future.”

entry.title: Parliament Representation Reflects Diversity
entry.summary:
DHAKA, Bangladesh, November 23 (IPS) - Whether financial power is now winning the chance to represent people in Parliament, one of the fundamental questions with regard to the future of democracy in Bangladesh is: Do regular people, especially those with limited economic means, have a fair chance of accessing politics and their voice in national decision-making? Parliament should not become an exclusive club for the rich nor a financial institution where money outweighs political experience, public faith and patriotism to serve the public. A trusted democratic system of representation is threatened by the increasing role played by rich and influential people in electoral politics.
